+    def self.write_back_nested(target, new_value, symtab)

+        symtab.add(target.name, Var.new(target.name, target.type(symtab), new_value))
body:
`write_back_nested` replaces the entire symbol table entry with a new `Var` via `symtab.add(...)`. This drops important `Var` metadata (e.g., `decode_var`, `param`, `for_loop_iter`, const-compatibility) and can also overwrite the existing object identity relied on elsewhere. Prefer updating the existing `Var` when present (e.g., `symtab.get(target.name).value = new_value`) and only `add` a new `Var` if the symbol truly does not exist.
```suggestion
        existing_var = symtab.get(target.name)
        if existing_var
          existing_var.value = new_value
        else
          symtab.add(target.name, Var.new(target.name, target.type(symtab), new_value))
        end
```
